claim: Coco M0 is memory for your AI coding tools: what you decided in one tool comes back in the next, at the moment you type your prompt.
Prompt-time recall: on a fixed live check of 10 questions, M0 brought back the right memory 10 times out of 10, returned nothing for both trick questions, and answered in 21 to 53 ms.
Nothing leaves your Mac: one local store, a daemon that only listens on your own machine, and no cloud model calls. Recall and the embedder are both off until you switch them on.

Works across tools: Claude Code turns are captured and recalled today; Cursor and Pi capture is in the current build and switches on one tool at a time; Antigravity's session-start recall is wired and in its first test.
A block list runs first: a name on your list is never saved, never recalled, and nothing is embedded when the list finds a hit.
Codex support: every finished Codex turn saved to M0. Built and tested, next to go live.
A read door for every tool: Cursor, Pi and others can list and open the notes you gave M0, through a local-only door that re-checks the block list on every line and caps each answer.
One-command wiring: M0 hooks into each tool's settings and never overwrites a setting that tool already has; removing a tool's hook leaves the rest untouched.
Private beta: in daily use, with prompt-time recall live across tools.
Launch window: no date yet. The public release follows its safety and recall gates.
